description: How a CVE JSON 5 affected entry's collectionURL names a package: the collection URL (matched as a prefix, case-insensitive, on a path boundary) -> the purl type its packageName is a name of, the namespace a distribution's names carry, the separator a collection writes between namespace and name (Maven's group:artifact), and whether the collection is a forge whose packageName is a repository (owner/name). The CVE record matcher compares the resulting package with each release's component purls (full namespace and name), and a forge repository with the release's source repository. A collection missing here names no package. Edit it by authoring a successor of the cve-applicability Procedure; keep the sources.
sources: https://cveproject.github.io/cve-schema/schema/docs/ (CVE JSON 5.1: affected[].collectionURL, packageName, repo, cpes; the collectionURL examples)
https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec/blob/main/PURL-TYPES.rst (purl types, their namespaces and name forms)
